sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of an incomplete but three-dimensionally preserved skeleton that includes parts of the skull, spine, forelimb and hindlimb.
The fossils were uncovered in 2023 by Hyemin Jo on Aphae Island in South Korea.
The generic name combines a Korean cartoon character with the Ancient Greek word for lizard, while the specific epithet honors paleontologist Min Huh for his work on Korean dinosaurs.
Doolysaurus is placed within the ornithischian clade Thescelosauridae, a family of small-to-medium herbivorous dinosaurs.
Phylogenetic studies consistently recover it as a member of the subfamily Thescelosaurinae.
It lived during the Albian to Cenomanian stages of the Cretaceous period, roughly the middle part of that era.
Its remains come from the Ilseongsan Formation of South Korea, which dates to the Albian to lower Cenomanian.
Analyses of its evolutionary relationships differ depending on the dataset used, with some studies placing Doolysaurus in Orodrominae and others in Thescelosaurinae.
